changes: The phone battery icon on the dash no longer shows an empty battery just after connecting: the level comes from Android's battery broadcast, and no icon is sent until there is a real reading
A new version is offered when you open the app, not only after the phone restarted
The Bluetooth device chosen for autostart (helmet intercom, headset, …) always starts KawaNav when it connects, also within the hour after you stopped it by hand
Ride distance uses the odometer and the GPS together: no more 1 km steps, and closer to the real distance
Rides saved before are worked out again when you open them or the riding log: their distance and average speed may change a little
A second ride recorded without restarting the app no longer starts with a jump in distance
No more −60 °C oil (or −40 °C coolant and intake) in the first seconds after connecting; such values in older rides are ignored
The instant fuel consumption's "no value" (102.3) is no longer recorded
Battery warnings no longer fire on one low reading while the fuel pump primes or just after a start, and can be turned off in Settings
The bike screen's total time is shown in hours and minutes: the dash reports minutes, not hours
The phone battery icon on the dash no longer flashes a low or unknown battery when Android briefly gives no reading
The bike's average and instant fuel economy can be shown in km/L, L/100 km, MPG US or MPG UK (L/100 km by default)
KawaNav is now a joint project of Darthbob and jackyes, with jackyes' features merged in
New look after Rideology: bottom bar with Home, Bike, record button, Rides and Settings; dark and light theme
Your bike: odometer, trips, fuel and range, battery voltage, temperatures, maintenance reminders and live values; the last values stay after the ignition is off, with "Walk to the bike"
Ride recording: GPS track and the bike's values, riding log with totals and records, ride summary with charts, export as Rideology CSV, GPX or all values
Refuel diary, 12 V battery log and maintenance log
Speed camera warnings from the offline map data (off by default)
Call and message icons and the clock on the dash (off by default)
Ride settings of the bike (riding mode, power, traction control…) shown in the app
In-app updates: KawaNav offers new versions with the list of changes and installs them (Android asks to confirm)
"What do the options mean?" under "Which curves count": explains each option and which arrow the dash shows
Shorter README with simpler install steps
Phone battery on the dash: 4 bars and charging, like with Rideology
Headset icon on the dash while your helmet intercom is connected
Warning in the app when the dash does not support turn-by-turn
Stop with autostart set up no longer reconnects after a few seconds
Pairing the bike in KawaNav is now tested: Rideology is not needed
First release: Google Maps directions and upcoming curves on the dash, autostart, offline maps
